newsitem.title: GERMANY: Protesters hold up nuclear waste train in Germany.
newsitem.headline: Protesters hold up nuclear waste train in Germany.

text.p: Anti-nuclear activists staged a sit-down protest on rail tracks in northern Germany on Monday, delaying a train carrying a controversial shipment of nuclear waste on its way to a storage depot.

Police deployed in Germany's biggest post-war security operation removed dozens of activists from the tracks just outside the city of Goettingen. The blockade delayed the nuclear train by 20 minutes as well as other rail traffic.

Officers lined the tracks wearing riot helmets and carrying batons while twelve police helicopters circled overhead. About 150 protesters were on the spot but only a few managed to slip between police lines to climb on to the tracks.

It was the first major delay for the train carrying six containers of spent nuclear fuel which left the southwestern town of Walheim early on Monday on its journey north to Gorleben medium-term storage depot, east of Hanover.

Authorities banned demonstrations along the route and the shipment was guarded by a total of 30,000 police across the country, concentrating their efforts around Goettingen and Gorleben to ensure its safe passage.
Green's leader Gunda Roestel told Saar radio her party valued the anti-nuclear waste protests as "a symbol against atomic energy policy in our country".
"There is only one alternative for the (government's energy) concept -- to abolish atomic power in the face of popular protest," Roestel said.
Opposition Social Democrats (SPD) criticised the government's energy policy, saying "the people" were against it because they realised it posed risks to health and environment.
